summary: Ancient citation refetch is independent and fail-closed. Modern position verification now also has a private/RLS page-level evidence schema, hash-verifying idempotent ingestion and a strict publication_id + page_ref fetcher; KG position text, claim text and biographies cannot substitute, and absent/unreviewed pages return MISSING. The migration is not deployed and no real protected secondary-page corpus has been backfilled, so current positions will intentionally remain unavailable rather than falsely verified.
resolution_criteria: Deploy the page-evidence migration; ingest lawful fingerprinted manifestations and visually reviewed printed/physical page concordances for every published modern position; verify each position against page text hashes; prove zero metadata fallback and pass the full adversarial GraphRAG suite on the immutable release. Ancient slug-to-corpus and translation-authority tests must remain green.

summary: Passage-slug verification previously fell back to the KG description that had fed synthesis, so a false or editorial description could verify itself. Passage slugs now require one exact corpus UUID mapping and fresh passages.text_content; ambiguity/missing mapping, non-citable roles and unauthorized or machine translations return MISSING and block publication.
resolution_criteria: No ancient passage verification path reads kg_nodes.description as source text; slug mapping is unique and exact; corpus role/language/citability and translation authority are enforced; adversarial tests remain green.

adjudication.decision: Treat passage slugs only as handles and re-fetch evidence from the uniquely mapped corpus UUID.
adjudication.rationale: Re-reading the same KG description is not independent verification. The corpus passage and its source-role metadata are the minimum independent runtime evidence surface.

summary: Nodes, edges and statistics previously described potentially different graph snapshots and totals. The API now exposes one deterministic release_id and served totals on every list/statistics response; live DB counts are separate diagnostics, reload swaps the in-process release, and the frontend rejects page mixing or count drift.
resolution_criteria: Every in-process nodes/edges/stats/reload response remains bound to the same deterministic release_id and served totals; live DB drift is explicit; frontend pagination rejects release changes; targeted contract tests pass.

adjudication.decision: Make the served in-memory snapshot, not live database counts, the pagination authority and identify it by deterministic SHA-256 release_id.
adjudication.rationale: A client can only paginate rows actually served by the process. Separating live asserted counts from served counts prevents silent truncation and false stale caused by derived inverse edges.

summary: Production currently exposes exactly one attested eleutheria-api container with one effective Uvicorn worker. PostgreSQL publication is atomic and the exact-SHA runbook recreates that single API only after the verified data swap; client, workspace and health release preconditions remain fail-closed. Multi-replica atomic cutover is not implemented and is explicitly outside this adjudication.
resolution_criteria: Adjudicated only for the attested single-public-API topology. Reopen before any second API container, load-balancer or tunnel upstream, independently reloadable worker, rolling/canary/blue-green deployment, or multi-process use of POST /api/kg/reload. A reopened issue requires direct candidate-replica enumeration, identical release_id and totals, atomic traffic shift, retained rollback replicas and a deterministic multi-replica integration gate.

adjudication.decision: Treat multi-replica release atomicity as not applicable to the currently attested single-container, single-worker production topology; do not claim multi-replica support.
adjudication.rationale: The secret-free live capture records one eleutheria-api container and one effective Uvicorn worker. The release runbook backs up PostgreSQL, publishes the five served tables atomically, recreates the sole API only after commit, verifies healthy DB/GraphRAG state and exact served totals, then requires eight public expected-release probes. Independent and adversarial reviews pass with explicit topology limits and reopen triggers; Cloudflare tunnel configuration was not inspected.

summary: The dynamic SPA fallback is now fail-closed noindex with no canonical, hreflang or JSON-LD; fictional locale alternates are removed, The Debate is prerendered, and CI runs the full prerender plus SEO contract. Cloudflare dynamic URLs still return HTTP 200 and valid entities still lack object-specific SSR/SSG, release-derived sitemaps and dereferenceable /kg IDs, so top-tier SEO/GEO remains incomplete. Public llms.txt and robots.txt now explicitly state incomplete verification, variable artifact licences and that crawler access is not a licence grant; the SEO contract rejects former zero-fabrication/all-CC claims.
resolution_criteria: Invalid IDs return real 404/410; valid public objects have server-rendered object-specific HTML/canonical/JSON-LD; sitemaps derive from the release; /kg/{id} is dereferenceable; crawler integration tests pass.

summary: The full test suites pass but emit PydanticGraphDeprecationWarning because ScholarlyAgent imports the deprecated BaseNode-style Graph runner; upstream states that this persistence/runner path will be removed or repurposed in v2.
resolution_criteria: Migrate the scholarly workflow and persistence semantics to the supported GraphBuilder API, or pin a reviewed compatible pydantic-graph major version with an explicit migration plan; remove the deprecation warning and pass the full GraphRAG, backend and root suites.
